$comment: publish[] (#794) is the publish table: one unit per releasable package (the 21 SDKs of .sdks[] plus sdk-shared), each naming its gate, registry (or none, with a reason), coordinates, versionSource and the units it must follow (after). tagFormat is the one release-tag shape; tools/sdk-pack/resolve-publish.mjs is the only reader that decides whether a tag may publish. liveSuite.runner (#783) is the ONE command that runs an SDK's live wire-cases: it always goes through the harness wrapper (`--corpus-seed --exec -- <cmd>`), which boots the harness, exports CONFEATURE_LIVE=1 + LIVE_HARNESS_URL and passes the exit code through — so no caller can run a live suite that silently skips. Nothing outside the wrapped command is a shell operator or substitution (`<wrapper> -- cmd || true` would make bash, not the wrapper, decide the leg; #926): an operator belongs inside a quoted `bash -c '…'`. The wrapper's `--corpus-seed` is each suite's declaration of the cases it must exercise: every seeded corpus case, and the wrapper fails a suite that sent no request for any of them, naming them (#926). Its one runner is the Dagger function `live-suite --sdk <name>` (#918), which runs it on that SDK's own toolchain as the second step of the SDK's sdk-gates.yml leg, after its suite, so a red live suite reddens the leg; a ci.native `macos` SDK (swift, #924) runs the same runner natively, in that job after its suite, through tools/repo-gates/run-live-suite.mjs; a `smoke` SDK cannot carry one (tools/repo-gates/select-sdks.mjs). Single source of truth for per-SDK containerized test coverage (spec 053 Phase 5, #204). Consumed by .github/workflows/release-gate.yml and .github/workflows/sdk-publish.yml. status=covered SDKs run their daggerFn as a publish/release gate; status=pending SDKs BLOCK publish (no false-green); status=exempt SDKs publish without a gate (documented reason). Flip a pending entry to covered (with its daggerFn) when epic #354 containerizes it — both gates auto-enroll it with zero workflow edits. localGate (default true when absent): whether the SDK also runs in the LOCAL prepushAll suite. Tier-2 SDKs (java/dotnet/php/ruby/rust/dart) are covered but localGate=false — release-gate-only — because 6 heavyweight heterogeneous toolchain containers in parallel exceed the NFR-004 8GB local budget (they OOM the Dagger engine); this is the constitution v1.3.0 'demote the slowest tier to release-gate-only' clause. The release-gate runs each on its own CI runner, so no shared-memory OOM. android + kotlin-mp (#364) are also localGate=false: their shared androidSdkContainer is pinned to linux/amd64 because AGP ships only an x86-64 aapt2 (no linux-aarch64 build), so on an arm64 host it runs under emulation — too slow for prepushAll, fine for the release gate. ci (#793) is how .github/workflows/sdk-gates.yml runs an SDK on every push and pull request: an SDK with a daggerFn runs it as a Dagger leg (`gate (<name>)`); an SDK whose daggerFn is null carries ci.native instead, `macos` (built and tested natively on a macos-15 runner) or `smoke` (a labelled source-quality smoke, not a build). Every SDK has exactly one of the two (tools/repo-gates/verify-workflows.mjs rule 19). ci.knownRed: `#<issue>` marks an SDK whose first run is red with a defect too large for its child: its leg runs in gate-known-red, shown red with the ticket and not counted, and a pull request honours the waiver only as the BASE commit carries it (tools/repo-gates/select-sdks.mjs), so a pull request cannot waive its own red. liveExempt: `<reason>` (#918) is why an SDK has no liveSuite, carried instead of a liveSuite with no runner, never beside one. Every SDK has one of the two since #924 (tools/test-harness-live-contract/tests/live-suite-runners.test.ts fails on an SDK with neither); live-coverage-report.mjs would list one as no live suite yet, never as covered.
